title: Ibn Sina (Avicenna)
summary: Ibn Sina, born near Bukhara in the 970s or 980, became a court physician and philosopher in Hamadan and Isfahan. His Canon of Medicine and the philosophical encyclopedia al-Shifa (The Cure) were widely read; the Latin Canon underpinned medical teaching in European universities until the 17th century. He died in Hamadan in 1037.

uncertainty.note: Birth year is uncertain: Stanford Encyclopedia says probably the 970s, possibly 964; MacTutor says 980. Death in 1037 is agreed.

as_recorded.value: some time in the 70s of the tenth century, perhaps as early as 964

where.modern_name: Bukhara area, Uzbekistan (born at a village near Bukhara; died at Hamadan, Iran)
where.historical_name: Afshana / Kharmaithen near Bukhara, Samanid emirate

importance.justification: Leading physician-philosopher of the medieval Islamic world whose Canon shaped medicine in the Islamic world and Europe.

sources.title: Abu Ali al-Husain ibn Abdullah ibn Sina (Avicenna)
